question: Let $A=\begin{bmatrix}1 & x \\ 2 & y \end{bmatrix}$ and $B=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 0 \\ 1 & 3 \end{bmatrix}$ be such that $AB = BA$. Determine the values of $x$ and $y$. Justify your solution by showing all steps and evaluating each stage for logic and potential errors.
explanation:
Compute $AB$ and $BA$:

$AB = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & x \\ 2 & y \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 3 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 1\cdot2 + x\cdot1 & 1\cdot0 + x\cdot3 \\ 2\cdot2 + y\cdot1 & 2\cdot0 + y\cdot3 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 + x & 3x \\ 4 + y & 3y \end{bmatrix}$

$BA = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 3 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} 1 & x \\ 2 & y \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 2\cdot1 + 0\cdot2 & 2\cdot x + 0\cdot y \\ 1\cdot1 + 3\cdot2 & 1\cdot x + 3\cdot y \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 2x \\ 1+6 & x + 3y \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 2x \\ 7 & x+3y \end{bmatrix}$

Set $AB = BA$:

Compare each element:

From position (1,1):
$2 + x = 2 \implies x = 0$

From position (1,2):
$3x = 2x \implies x = 0$

From position (2,1):
$4 + y = 7 \implies y = 3$

From position (2,2):
$3y = x + 3y \implies x = 0$

Thus, $x = 0$ and $y = 3$.

Check:

If $x = 0$, $y = 3$:

$A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 3 \end{bmatrix}$

$AB = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 3 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 3 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0 \\ 4 + 3 & 2\cdot0+3\cdot3 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0 \\ 7 & 9 \end{bmatrix}$

$BA = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 3 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 3 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 2\cdot1 + 0\cdot2 & 2\cdot0 + 0\cdot3 \\ 1\cdot1 + 3\cdot2 & 1\cdot0 + 3\cdot3 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0 \\ 1 + 6 & 9 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0 \\ 7 & 9 \end{bmatrix}$

Hence, $AB = BA$ for $x = 0, y = 3$ (verified).

Conclusion:
$x = 0, y = 3$ are the required values.
